12.  Which process will increase the entropy of the local surroundings?
A.  The melting of a block of ice
B.  Evaporation of water vapour
C.  The isothermal expansion of a gas
D.  The adiabatic expansion of a gas
questions.text_clean:
Which process will increase the entropy of the local surroundings?
A. The melting of a block of ice
B. Evaporation of water vapour
C. The isothermal expansion of a gas
D. The adiabatic expansion of a gas
questions.review_note: Key C. Isothermal expansion of a gas requires heat Q to flow INTO the gas from the surroundings, so the entropy of the surroundings decreases (by Q/T); the gas's own entropy increases. A and B likewise absorb heat from the surroundings and D exchanges none, so no option increases the entropy of the surroundings as worded. The key appears to read 'surroundings' as the system; item is flawed.

A black body has absolute temperature $T$ and surface area $A$. The intensity of the radiation emitted by the body is $I$. Another black body of surface area $2A$ has absolute temperature $2T$. What is the intensity of radiation emitted by this second black body?
A. $4I$
B. $8I$
C. $16I$
D. $32I$
questions.review_note: Key D (32I) treats 'intensity' as total emitted power ($\sigma A T^4$ scaled by 2 x 16). Intensity as power per unit area depends only on $T^4$, giving 16I (option C). The question deliberately changes the area, so the key's 32I is only correct if intensity means total power.
